title: Funnel-led Pricing + Velocity Scratch
content:
Goal: quick, back-of-envelope model for a funnel-first pricing approach that charges for activation velocity + sustained usage. Aim: capture value of early-engagement while protecting unit economics for high-throughput customers.

Context notes
- Problem: strictly per-token pricing underprices onboarding spikes and leads to too-high initial cost for viral flows. Need a way to encourage trial and trial-to-paid conversion without subsidizing long tail of abusive/low-value spikes.
- Idea: small activation retainer (per-account) that covers N initial tokens / session starts in a 30d window + pay-as-you-go above. Retainer size pegged to expected conversion funnel and amortized across cohorts.

Assumptions (rough)
- Infra cost basis: $0.06/GPU-minute effective (amortized across infra + ops); more conservative for high memory models.
- Throughput baseline: optimized quantized model yields 100 tokens/sec per GPU for mixed seq lengths (short + medium).
- Average prompt+response = 800 tokens per session (rough for multi-turn search + summary combos).
- Effective tokens per GPU-hour = 100 tokens/sec * 3600 = 360k tokens/hour -> cost per token = (0.06 * 60) / 360k ??? WAIT re-eval: 0.06/GPU-minute = $3.6/GPU-hour. So cost per token = $3.6 / 360k = $0.00001/token (1e-5).
- Add overheads (routing, control plane, cache storage, infra ops): multiply by 2.5 => blended infra unit cost = $0.000025/token. Add margin target 3x => floor price ~ $0.000075/token. This is baseline PAYG purely infra-backed.

Funnel-led construct (quick sketch)
- Activation retainer: $25 covers first 100k tokens or 30 session starts (whichever first) during first 30 days.
  * Rationale: $25 retainer amortized against cost: 100k tokens * infra unit cost $0.000025 = $2.5 infra. Leaves room to subsidize other costs (customer success, onboarding) and to incentivize conversion.
- Post-retainer PAYG: $0.00007/token base (matches floor calc but competitive).
- Velocity multiplier for bursts: during day-0->7, allow 5x burst capacity but apply 1.5x token rate for any tokens above 250k/day to discourage abuse.
- Committed-monthly option (startups scaling): $1,500/month reserve -> includes 10M tokens + 99.9% SLA and priority rollout. Effective committed per-token = $0.00015/token, but discounts/credits for steady daily baseline traffic and reduced overage rates.

Example customer scenarios
1) Small app testing (trial)
- Activation retainer $25 covers them for likely trial usage (1–3k sessions). If they convert to paid and use 1M tokens/month, they pay: retainer consumed + 900k * $0.00007 = $63 => month1 total ~ $88. Unit economics: infra cost = 1M * 0.000025 = $25 -> gross margin good.

2) Mid-market SaaS with conversational product (5M tokens/mo)
- If PAYG: 5M * $0.00007 = $350; infra cost = 5M * 0.000025 = $125 -> gross margin 64%. If they choose commit (e.g., $5k/mo for 40M tokens committed) we can give lower per-token and guaranteed capacity.

3) Viral burst (freemium product)
- The retainer helps gate the very earliest spikes. Velocity multiplier and burst bucket pricing makes sustained viral loops expensive unless team converts or buys a burst package. This reduces tail subsidy.

Session-bundles variant (alternative)
- Instead of token-first, sell session-bundles: 100 sessions = $X. Useful for short-prompt high-turnover apps. Need to carefully define session: TTL vs inactivity window vs token cap.
- For our average 800 tokens/session, 100 sessions ~ 80k tokens -> price should be ~80k * $0.00007 = $5.6 + markup => sell $9–12/100-sessions. Could fit small mobile app pricing $9/mo starter.

Open questions / TODO
- Recompute infra unit cost for different model classes (bfloat16 vs 8-bit quant) — delta can be 2–4x. Need param table for small, medium, large open models.
- How to measure value-per-session? Determine conversion uplift from session quality improvements; tie to ability to charge higher retainers for high-precision models.
- Decide default session definition: 5 min idle TTL vs 30 min. Impacts session-bundle economics a lot.
- Product engineering work: implement activation retainer lifecycle (apply credit, expiration, conversion credits). Linked ticket: PRIC-77.
- Fraud/abuse: need heuristics for automated refund of retained credits in clear abuse cases.

Edge-case math (fast checks)
- If model choice increases token cost by 3x (e.g., LlamaX large -> tokens cost $0.000075 infra), then blended price at 3x margin = $0.000225/token. Our retainer should scale (e.g., cover fewer tokens) or add model-surcharge flag.
- Break-even retainer sizing: target retainer to cover COGS + onboarding S&M per new paying account in cohort. If cohort CAC = $120 and onboarding S&M allocated at $40/account, retainer should be at least $40 (or priced below with expectation to recoup).

Decision points for next PRD iteration
- Default funnel retainer: $25 (covers 100k tokens) vs alternative $50 covering 250k. Run cohort sim with existing funnel metrics to see which better preserves conversion.
- Velocity enforcement: soft (rate-limits + warnings) vs hard (billing multiplier). Prefer soft during early experiments.
- Bundles: test session-bundle $9/100-sessions vs token-based starter $25/100k tokens. A/B with sales teams.

Quick experiment plan
- Pick two cohorts (organic signups vs invited beta users). Randomize starter plan: (A) $25 retainer 100k tokens; (B) $50 retainer 250k tokens. Track 30/60 day conversion, average tokens in first 30d, churn. If conversion delta < 5% and cost delta > X, prefer cheaper retainer.
- Instrument metrics: tokens/day/per-account, sessions/day/per-account, avg-token-length, model-selection share.

Notes to self
- Keep pricing language simple: "Starter credit" not "retainer" when talking to devs.
- Document default session TTL and visible usage meter in console.
- Follow up with infra team for precise per-model per-seq-length token cost matrix to replace back-of-envelope assumptions.

Rough TL;DR (for Slack)
- Proposal: price starter activation credit ($25 -> 100k tokens) + post-credit PAYG $0.00007/token. Offer commit discounts for monthly reserved pools. Use velocity-based multipliers to discourage sustained viral spikes without conversion. Run small randomized experiment to validate conversion lift and net unit economics.

--end of scratchpad (lots of TODOs).
